subject: Post-call: LLM suitability assessment + benchmark pack — Orion Analytics
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@orion-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: LLM suitability assessment + benchmark pack — Orion Analytics

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we have a single place to iterate:

What we heard
- Primary workload: multi-turn summarization + classification for analyst notes (avg prompt 180 tokens, response target 120–200 tokens).
- Quality priority: factuality for extractive answers and low hallucination on numeric fields.
- Latency target: 200–350ms p50 for interactive UI; throughput bursts ~60 qps for end-of-day batch tasks.
- Data posture: sensitive PII in prompts; you prefer Private or Dedicated deployment.

Redwood recommendations (shortlist)
1) RW-Lite-7B-q4 (quantized) — best cost/latency balance for user-facing UIs. Redwood-verified profile: 75 TPS sustained (batching), p50 120ms, p95 420ms on a single A10G with continuous batching.
2) RWX-13B-v1 (fp16) — higher-quality answering and lower hallucination on open-domain prompts. Profile: 28 TPS sustained, p50 210ms, p95 560ms.
3) RW-ULTRA-70B (sharded fp16) — for aggressive quality/regression-sensitive endpoints; profile: 6 TPS sustained, p50 480ms, p95 1.2s.

Links & artifacts I shared
- Redwood-verified performance profiles and raw metrics: https://console.redwood.ai/benchmarks/ORN-2027/suite-20270403
- Suggested prompt set (sample): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBz-Orion-eval-prompts
- Mutual action plan (initial): attached spreadsheet

Quality/regression notes
- Quantized variants (q4) reduce compute cost ~2.5x but we typically see a small uptick in LLM hallucination on long-context numerical synthesis tasks. We flagged representative prompts from your sample where RW-Lite-7B-q4 produced subtle number-format errors; we'll include these in the eval harness.

Proposed next steps (pick whichever fits):
- We run a 1k-case eval of your prompt set across RW-Lite-7B-q4 and RWX-13B-v1 (we'll return ROC curves, confusion matrix for labels, and hallucination-rate sampling).
- If you want to prioritize latency/cost, run a 5k synthetic batch to measure steady-state TPS under your burst profile.
- Schedule a 30-min follow-up next Tue to review results + discuss Dedicated vs Private pricing and deployment SLOs.

Can you confirm 1) the prompt set link above is final, and 2) whether procurement should be looped now (I cc'd procurement address per your comment)?

Best,
Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: rnwd_bench_ORN_summary.pdf (summary), orc_mvp_mutual_action_plan.xlsx (MVP checklist)

From: Elena Park <elena.park@orion-analytics.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Turner <mike.turner@orion-analytics.com>, procurement@orion-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2027 18:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: LLM suitability assessment + benchmark pack — Orion Analytics

Hi Sergio —

Thanks for the clear recap and the benchmarking links. A few quick notes from our side:

- Prompt set: I'm uploading the full prompt set (1.2k items) to the Drive folder you shared; file is named Orion_prompt_set_v1.jsonl. That contains our core PII-masked examples and some edge cases with numerical tables.
- Primary concern: hallucination on numeric synthesis and table extraction. Any quantization-induced regressions are a blocker for production unless we can show parity on the critical numeric tests.
- Deployment: we prefer Redwood Dedicated inside a single dedicated region for now; we'll evaluate Private later once integration and compliance are validated.

Request: Can you run the 1k-case eval specifically focused on the 200 numeric-critical items and provide:
  * hallucination rate metric (as % of tests with incorrect numeric output)
  * example negatives with prompt/response pairs (5 high-severity examples)
  * latency distribution for both interactive and batch shapes

Procurement (cc'd) — once we confirm the fit, what information do you need from us to start a PO?

Thanks,
Elena Park
Head of ML Product, Orion Analytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@orion-analytics.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, procurement@orion-analytics.com
Date: Sat, 4 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: LLM suitability assessment + benchmark pack — Orion Analytics

Hi Elena —

Happy to run the eval. Proposed execution plan:

1) Quick sanity run (today) — 200 numeric-critical items across RW-Lite-7B-q4 and RWX-13B-v1 to surface immediate regressions. Deliverable: scoreboard CSV + 5 high-severity prompt/response pairs.
2) Full 1k run (48h) — all prompts in Orion_prompt_set_v1.jsonl for the three shortlisted models (RW-Lite-7B-q4, RWX-13B-v1, RW-ULTRA-70B). Deliverable: full report with: hallucination-rate, token-level diff stats, latency p10/p50/p95, and ROC/PR where applicable.
3) Canary recommendation — if RW-Lite-7B-q4 shows <1.2% severe numeric-hallucination on the 200 set, recommend canary to Dedicated with 100 RPS cap and automatic rollback on hallucination-regression >1.5% at 95% CI.

Procurement note: for a Dedicated MVP we typically need a signed MSA + PO. I attached a sample SOW line items and the mutual action plan (orc_mvp_mutual_action_plan.xlsx). For an initial Dedicated commitment we can scope a 3-month reserve to match your burst profile; I'll have Laura follow up on pricing once the evaluation completes.

Sergio — copying next available slots: Tue 2027-04-06 10:00 PT or Wed 2027-04-07 14:00 PT for the review. Which works for you and Elena?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@orion-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, procurement@orion-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: LLM suitability assessment + benchmark pack — Orion Analytics

Elena / Mike / procurement team —

Great, thanks for the signal. We'll kick off the sanity run now and target delivery of the 200-item scoreboard by EOD tomorrow (Sat we have a small ops window but Marissa will start the run and we will ship interim results).

Immediate asks from procurement to accelerate PO:
- Signed MSA (I will send the current MSA template to procurement after this thread).
- Billing contact + legal contact for standard security addenda (we support KMS integrations and SOC2 evidence; Laura, can you share the quick SOC2 checklist to procurement?).

Elena — we'll surface the 5 high-severity examples in the initial report and include the raw logs (redacted PII) and the specific prompt/response pairs so your QA can triage. After the 1k run we can produce a comparison PDF optimized for execs showing p50/p95 latency by model and expected monthly unit cost.

Confirmed follow-up: Tue 2027-04-06 10:00 PT. I'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Orion_prompt_set_v1.jsonl (uploaded by Elena, referenced), rnwd_bench_ORN_summary.pdf (attached), orc_mvp_mutual_action_plan.xlsx (attached)
